extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal financial assistance (elementary, secondary, and postsecondary institutions), Title IX Coordinators, institutional legal counsel, and other stakeholders responding to or implementing Title IX regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes the regulatory standards, obligations, and guidance in the Department of Education's Title IX final rule preamble that recipients must follow (policies, grievance procedures, training, recordkeeping, coordinator duties, scope of discrimination). Useful for institutions implementing or commenting on Title IX requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement: voluntary correction before termination or DOJ referral
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department recognizes that it cannot pursue termination of Federal financial assistance or refer a matter to the Department of Justice unless a recipient refuses to voluntarily correct a violation after the Department has notified the recipient of the violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites statutory/regulatory authority (20 U.S.C. 1682; 34 CFR 100.8). This frames OCR enforcement as generally relying first on notification and opportunities for voluntary correction before pursuing termination or DOJ referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicizing OCR case resolutions
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR makes resolution agreements available to the public on its website in a searchable database by name of recipient or by protected category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department considers OCR's existing public database sufficient to inform the public and will continue to highlight specific notable cases through other means as appropriate (example link provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely resolution of complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department strives to resolve cases efficiently but recognizes that OCR's necessary case processing time will vary based on many factors, including the allegations and facts presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No safe harbor for partial compliance was adopted because the Department considers full compliance necessary to meet statutory objectives. The Department declines to add additional penalties or deterrence mechanisms without public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of regulatory provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each provision of the final regulations is intended to operate independently; severability clauses in part 106 (including specific sections listed) continue to be applicable so invalidity of one provision should not affect others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: prohibition on retaliation (§106.71) and application of Title IX to sex-based hostile environments (§106.11) operate independently of each other and other provisions; the Department included this discussion to remove doubt that it would adopt remaining provisions even if one is struck down.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedure: objective evaluation; prohibition on status-based credibility determinations (§106.45(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must require an objective evaluation of all evidence that is relevant and not otherwise impermissible and must prohibit credibility determinations based on a person's status as a complainant, respondent, or witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specific procedural requirement is emphasized as operating separately from scope clarifications of sex discrimination, reinforcing that fair process obligations exist regardless of other definitional or scope changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of sex discrimination: bases vs forms (§106.10, §106.2, §106.31(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation lists bases of discrimination that involve consideration of sex—sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation, and gender identity—which are distinct from forms of sex discrimination (e.g., sex-based harassment, sexual violence, prevention of participation consistent with gender identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that the listed bases are separate from the various forms of sex discrimination that may occur, and the regulations address both bases and forms in different sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must comply with regulations in their entirety (no partial safe harbor)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to include a safe harbor for recipients that address sex-based harassment but do not comply with all of the requirements in the final regulations because it is important for all recipients to comply with the regulations in their entirety to ensure statutory objectives are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes comprehensive compliance rather than permitting partial implementation as sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact estimate: anticipated increase in investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department estimates that inclusion of the additional bases of sex discrimination within the scope of the Title IX regulations may result in a 10 percent increase in the number of investigations conducted annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This estimate informed cost calculations; commenters did not provide data to change it. Costs related to any increased litigation were acknowledged but not found to be extensive based on available data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative size standard for small entities (use of enrollment)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of assessing impacts on small entities, the Department uses enrollment as the basis for defining 'small institutions of higher education (IHE)' rather than adopting the SBA revenue standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department explains methodology and declines to adopt a $7,000,000 revenue threshold for small LEAs/IHEs; acknowledges that the enrollment-based assumption (each small IHE conducts same number of investigations on average) likely overstates costs for the smallest entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of nondiscrimination publication requirements (§106.8): short-form option and format flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations require recipients to provide a notice of nondiscrimination but allow recipients the option to provide a short-form notice (a one-sentence statement that the recipient prohibits sex discrimination and that individuals may report concerns to the Title IX Coordinator, with a link to the full notice). Recipients may include the notice in print or electronically consistent with how materials are distributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This flexibility accounts for space/format limitations and aims to reduce burden. The Department also revised its burden estimate by increasing the hours for a Title IX Coordinator to review and revise policies from 6 to 12 hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements (§106.8(d)): timing and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Training must be provided promptly upon hiring or upon a change of position that alters an employee's duties under Title IX, and annually thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training obligations for employees with notification duties are accounted for in cost models; the Department considers the information employees must learn straightforward and incorporable into existing training. The Department adjusted estimates for Title IX Coordinator time accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirements (§106.8(f)): narrowed scope and access to training materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department removed the proposed requirement that recipients maintain all records documenting actions taken to meet obligations under §§106.40 and 106.57. The final regulations require recipients to make training materials available upon request for inspection by the public rather than making them publicly posted on the website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These changes were made to relieve administrative burden, though the Department retained its burden estimate to ensure capture of recordkeeping costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Title IX to hostile environments with extraterritorial conduct (§106.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.11 requires a recipient to address a sex-based hostile environment under its education program or activity even when some conduct alleged to be contributing to the hostile environment occurred outside of the recipient's education program or activity or outside the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that §106.11 does not require recipients to investigate conduct that occurred outside the United States; rather, it requires addressing hostile environments in the recipient's program that may have contributions from extraterritorial conduct. Department lacked basis to estimate costs for this change and expects a small number of such investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to address sex discrimination and notification standard (§106.44): removal of actual knowledge and reporting threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification requirements were modified to require that an employee with notification duties take action when the employee has information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part. The Department removed the 'actual knowledge' requirement for sexual harassment allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs associated with notification duties are considered part of training expenses; other costs related to duty to address sex discrimination are considered part of the Title IX Coordinator's duties. The Department states these changes do not require restriction of constitutionally protected speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator obligations: duty to monitor for barriers to reporting (§106.44(b) and (f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators have a role to monitor their education programs and activities for barriers to reporting sex discrimination, centralize duties, promote accountability, and enable effective Title IX compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department suggests low-cost monitoring methods (incorporating questions into existing training, roundtables, listening sessions) and de minimis corrective steps (reminders of reporting options, reporting employees who discourage reporting). Recipients may delegate duties to designees provided one Coordinator retains ultimate oversight. Department considered commenters' concerns about burden but retained flexibility for recipients to choose appropriate strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures requirement (§106.44(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations require a recipient to offer and coordinate supportive measures as appropriate, which may include counseling for a party who is experiencing suicidal ideation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is noted in response to comments about availability of mental health supports; supportive measures are part of the duty to address sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation: Title IX cannot require sex offender registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department does not have authority under Title IX to require individuals found responsible for sexual assault to register as sex offenders because sex offender registration is governed by other Federal, State, or local laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains scope limitation and that certain commenter suggestions (e.g., mandatory registration) are outside Title IX authority.
